transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~34 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Sienna CISO), Arjun Patel (Sienna Head of ML), Samir Rao (Procurement), Nora Lin (Legal)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side, I'm Lena, AE, and Diego is our systems engineer who will take the technical bits.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Hi all, Maya here. we wanted a focused session on how you handle data residency, the KMS flows, and most importantly—do you use customer prompts to train models, like at all?
[00:28] Diego Martinez: Good question, Maya. Short answer: we do not train on customer data by default. Redwood Hosted does not feed customer-provided request/response pairs back into model training pipelines. that's a policy and an enforced config.
[00:40] Arjun Patel: When you say "not train", is that contractual? is there an escape clause for opt-in analytics? how is it enforced?
[00:52] Lena Park: We can add explicit language in the contract — redwood provides a 'no-training' clause for enterprise customers. we'll send sample wording. It's also enforced at the platform level: customer data tags, separate buckets, and no ingestion to our training buckets.
[01:08] Samir Rao: And what about pseudonymization or redaction for PII/PHI? Our compliance requires that sensitive tokens are either not logged or are redacted.
[01:20] Diego Martinez: Audit logs and request logs are configurable. by default we store request metadata and token counts, not full prompt contents in long-term logs for enterprise plans, but for compliance we offer an option where full content is captured for X days only and then auto-pruned. we also integrate with customer KMS for envelope encryption so customer-managed keys can decrypt logs if they choose.
[01:42] Maya Chen: Wait—so full content can be captured temporarily. That raises concerns for us. We need assurance that PHI is never used and retention windows are strict. Show me the retention settings.
[01:57] Diego Martinez: Right—by default hosted paid tier: content retention is 30 days for diagnostics, but for enterprise with VPC/private it's configurable to zero retention. we documented the retention policy in the compliance FAQ. we'll send that doc.
[02:12] Arjun Patel: Another point: we run a model evaluation pipeline internally—if we were to test Redwood in EU region, can you guarantee the data never leaves the EU region for any processing including caching?
[02:27] Lena Park: Yes, we have EU regions with regional routing. requests provisioned to eu-west-1 are served from that region; fallbacks are also region-aware and won't cross borders unless explicitly allowed in routing policy. there's an option to disable cross-region failover.
[02:45] Nora Lin: From a contractual perspective, we need evidence: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 (if you have), and audit logs samples. do you provide a redacted SOC report?
[02:58] Lena Park: We can provide SOC 2 Type II attestation and an ISO 27001 certificate snapshot. we'll send a redacted report through our secure docs link.
[03:10] Maya Chen: Good. On encryption—how does KMS integrate? customer keys, HSM compatibility? we use a managed KMS at our cloud provider and we want customer key control.
[03:23] Diego Martinez: We support customer-managed keys via Cloud KMS or HSMs for Private deployments and Dedicated. For hosted, we offer an envelope encryption flow where the customer key encrypts the data encryption keys. We also support bring-your-own-HSM for Private. There's a runbook for integration.
[03:40] Arjun Patel: And does the KV cache or tokenizer caches hold any plaintext that could reconstitute PII?
[03:52] Diego Martinez: KV cache is stored in memory and encrypted at rest. we avoid persisting raw prompts to decentralized caches. there are short lived caches for latency, and we can configure stricter policies—zero-persist mode—if needed. sometimes transcription notes will say K-V cash which is funny—sorry if transcripts mis-spell.
[04:08] Samir Rao: We also need RBAC details—can you map to our internal AD groups and enforce least privilege for token issuance?
[04:19] Lena Park: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning so roles in Redwood can be tied to your AD groups. tokens can be scoped per role and token issuance audited.
[04:31] Maya Chen: What about audit log retention and SIEM integration? we need logs forwarded to our Splunk for 7 years for some of our funds.
[04:42] Diego Martinez: We can stream audit logs to customer endpoints or to an S3/secure bucket; retention policies are configurable. long-term retention for seven years is possible if you maintain them in your storage; Redwood can provide the export pipeline and sign them. we don't recommend storing full PII in logs though.
[04:59] Arjun Patel: Is the streaming real-time? do you guarantee delivery?
[05:06] Diego Martinez: We support near real-time forwarding with delivery guarantees at-least-once. for critical audits we recommend using our dedicated pipeline.
[05:16] Lena Park: Let's cover the legal ask—Nora, what exact phrasing do you want around training?
[05:23] Nora Lin: We want a clause that says 'Redwood shall not use, access, or incorporate Customer Data into model training, model improvement, or derivative models without explicit written consent.' ideally with an audit right and ability to require deletion of any retained training artifacts.
[05:38] Lena Park: That's reasonable. Redwood enterprise contracts typically include a similar clause; we'll have legal draft language and include an audit mechanism.
[05:45] Maya Chen: Also need to confirm whether embeddings or vectors derived from prompts are considered 'customer artifacts' that you might use for improvement.
[05:55] Diego Martinez: We treat any customer-derived vectors as customer property and, for enterprise/private, never ingest them into our public training pipelines. For hosted standard accounts, we have an opt-out control. We'll send a short note clarifying vectors/embeddings handling.
[06:12] Samir Rao: From procurement side, pricing for the EU pilot and any SLA implications? We need latency objectives and if you breach residency, what remedies exist.
[06:24] Lena Park: We can provide EU pilot pricing and SLA addendum covering region-specific obligations. For residency breaches we include remediation steps and credit frameworks; details to be provided in the SOW.
[06:35] Arjun Patel: Technical deep-dive request: can Diego show us the KMS key rotation flow and how audit logs tie to request IDs? we'd like to map traceability from request to storage object to key ID.
[06:49] Diego Martinez: Absolutely — we'll block 60 minutes for that next week. In that session I can demo a live request, show envelope encryption in action, and export a sample audit trail linking request ID -> storage object -> key fingerprint.
[07:02] Nora Lin: For evidence, also include a sample redacted audit log and the schema. we need to verify the fields.
[07:12] Diego Martinez: we'll include the schema and a redacted sample.
[07:18] Maya Chen: One more quick question—what's your policy on backups and cold storage? Are backups encrypted with the same CKMS?
[07:29] Diego Martinez: Backups are encrypted, and for Private/Dedicated we can configure them to use the customer's KMS. For hosted, we use managed keys but can also support customer-managed keys for enterprise.
[07:44] Lena Park: Okay, recap: Redwood will send SOC 2 Type II attestation, ISO snapshot, compliance FAQ, retention policy doc, KMS runbook, sample audit logs, and proposed contractual language for 'no-training'. Diego will schedule the technical deep dive. Any other items?
[07:59] Maya Chen: No, that covers it. we'll review the materials and if things look good we'll spin up an EU pilot environment.
[08:07] Samir Rao: We'll also need a procurement timeline—end of month ideally.
[08:13] Lena Park: Great—Lena out. thanks everyone.

[End of meeting]

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution errors and filler words remain. Some tech terms transcribed as phonetics like 'K-V cash' or 'V-C-P' in automated notes. The team will attach native docs in follow-up."
